title: The loop that removes consumed effects (`for e in acc.consumed: e.owner.remove_effect(e)`) is now copied in four places: creature._finish, combat attack, spells spell attack and damage.death_save. Pull it into one helper on the accumulator or in effects.py

history.summary: I moved the consumed-effects removal loop into one helper, `Acc.remove_consumed()` in `dungdra/effects.py`. The four copies now call it: `creature._finish`, the combat attack roll, the spell attack roll and `damage.death_save`. Behaviour is unchanged: the helper ends each effect in `acc.consumed` that still has an owner. I added two unit tests in `tests/unit/test_effects.py`. One checks that only consumed effects are removed. The other checks that an effect with no owner is skipped. The ticket lists no acceptance tests. The full suite passes (547 tests), ruff check and ruff format --check are clean, and dev-gate passes. This changes no SRD rule, so I added no SRD tags.
